prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
Our provision for credit losses was $40.6 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $4.5 million compared to a provision of $45.1 million for the third quarter of 2025. In addition, the provision for credit losses on non-fintech loans was $0.7 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to provision expense of $5.8 million in the third quarter of 2025 driven by estimated losses for the direct leasing portfolio in the third quarter of 2025 .

The fintech loan provision correlates to the amount of related non-interest income from a credit enhancement contractually provided by a third party. Accordingly, there was no related net impact from these amounts. See further discussion of this program in “ Financial Condition—Allowance for Credit Losses—Fintech Programs ” in MD&A.

For more information about our provision, allowance and credit loss experience, see “Financial Condition—Portfolio Performance” below and “Note 5. Loans, net” to the Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.

nonint.heading: Non-Interest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table presents the principal categories of non-interest expense for the periods indicated:

Total non-interest expense was $63.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $7.1 million, or 12.6%, compared to $56.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase is primarily driven by higher costs in the third quarter of 2026, including $4.3 million of costs related to the restructuring of our Small Business Lending business line and other departmental reductions, and $1.9 million related to an accrual for the estimated cost of a legal settlement.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense for the third quarter of 2026 increased $3.3 million to $45.5 million from $42.2 million in the third quarter of 2025, driven by $4.6 million higher interest on short-term borrowings and $1.4 million higher interest expense on senior debt, partially offset by $2.7 million lower interest expense on deposits.

Interest expense on deposits was $2.7 million lower, primarily driven by lower rates in 2026. In terest expense on short-term borrowings was $4.6 million higher in 2026, as that funding source was utilized to fund higher average loans on balance sheet in the third quarter of 2026, compared to limited utilization in third quarter of 2025. Interest expense on senior debt was $1.4 million higher, due to higher outstanding principal and higher rate on senior debt. In August 2025, $200 million of 7.375% Senior Notes due 2030 were issued, the proceeds of which were used in part to repay at maturity the $100 million of outstanding 4.75% Senior notes due 2025.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Income tax expense was $8.9 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $18.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. Our effective tax rate was 12.5% and 24.9% in the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, respectively, with each period based on a 21% federal tax rate, the impact of various state income taxes and the third quarter of 2026 was favorably impacted by purchased tax credits.

In third quarter of 2026, as part of our tax strategy, we purchased transferable tax credits to reduce our cash tax obligation for 2026 and certain eligible prior years. Income tax expense for the third quarter of 2026 includes $10.3 million of total benefits related to transferable investment tax credits, of which $3.0 million relates to 2026 taxes and $7.3 million relates to carryback of credits to prior periods. We expect to continue to invest in tax credits in future periods, resulting in an estimated annual future effective tax rate of approximately 23.9%, compared to the full year 2025 effective tax rate of 24.7%.

net.text: Our net income increased to $62.8 million in the third quarter of 2026 from $54.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of $7.9 million, or 14.3%.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Our net interest income for the third quarter of 2026 decreased $4.1 million, or 4.4%, to $90.1 million from $94.2 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Growth of Fintech Lending. Our strategy is to continue to drive growth in our Fintech lending business, as seen by the shift in mix to Fintech representing 19.6% of our total average loan portfolio in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 9.6% for the third quarter of 2025. A significant portion of these loans are zero percent interest and, as such, do not recognize interest income ; however , we do generate fee revenue from these loans, through our partnership agreements. This mix shift to non-interest earning loans results in a reduction of the calculated average rate earned by total loans, average rate earned by our total interest-earning assets, and net interest margin in the above analysis.

intro.text: The Bancorp, Inc. (the “Company,” “we,” “us,” “our” or “the holding company”) is a Delaware financial holding company and our primary, wholly-owned subsidiary is The Bancorp Bank , National Association (the “Bank”). The Bank is a federally chartered commercial bank located in Sioux Falls, South Dakota and is a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (“FDIC”) insured institution. The vast majority of our revenue and income is generated through the Bank. As described more fully below, our business strategy is focused on Fintech Solutions, including program sponsorship, payment services, and sponsored lending. We expect our fintech business to generate non-interest income and attract stable, lower cost deposits which we then seek to deploy into lower risk assets in specialized markets through the specialty lending activities of our Credit Solutions business.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
